title: Inverse Theory of Mind Modeling for Content Recommendation: From Web Browsing to Dynamic Intelligent Interfaces
abstract: arXiv:2608.11354v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Modern recommender systems treat observed actions as reliable proxies for user preferences, yet interactions often reflect exploration or comparison rather than stable preference expression. As interfaces evolve from static layouts toward generative UIs and immersive extended reality (XR), the need for deeper, modality-agnostic user understanding grows: these adaptive environments must decide not only what to present but where, when, how prominently, and most importantly why a user acts. We propose an Inverse Theory of Mind (IToM) pipeline that reasons backward from observed interactions to infer the beliefs, preferences, and decision-making traits that explain behavior. translated_title: 面向内容推荐的反向心智理论建模：从网页浏览到动态智能界面
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.11354v1 公告类型：新论文 摘要：现代推荐系统将观察到的行为视为用户偏好的可靠代理，但交互往往反映探索或比较，而非稳定的偏好表达。随着界面从静态布局向生成式用户界面和沉浸式扩展现实（XR）演进，对更深层次、模态无关的用户理解需求日益增长：这些自适应环境不仅必须决定呈现什么内容，还要决定在哪里、何时、以何种显著性呈现，以及最重要的是用户为何采取行动。我们提出了一种反向心智理论（IToM）流程，该流程从观察到的交互反向推理，以推断解释行为的信念、偏好和决策特征。该流程重建每个用户的决策上下文，包括选择了什么以及有哪些替代选项，应用基于LLM的反事实推理生成有证据依据的自然语言信念陈述，并通过多模态综合这些信念。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种反向心智理论（IToM）流程，通过从用户观察行为反向推理其信念、偏好和决策特征，以提升推荐系统对用户深层理解的准确性和适应性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an Inverse Theory of Mind (IToM) pipeline that reasons backward from observed user interactions to infer beliefs, preferences, and decision-making traits, enhancing recommender systems' deep and adaptive user understanding.
